Article Title: Meta cites 'error' after PM Modi's Facebook video briefly disappears

Article Title: Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as Union education minister amid massive student protests
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most critical factor in shaping India's education system? Inclusivity Quality of education Access to resources Student feedback 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday tendered his resignation from the Council of Ministers amid the ongoing protests over the NEET paper leak.In a letter addressed to his "young friends," Pradhan said that he has sent his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi , considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country."I have been dedicated to students, teachers, and education reform for more than four decades. I have always believed that a strong, inclusive, and visionary education system is the very foundation of a strong nation. I deeply respect the aspirations, emotions, and just expectations of the country's youth. Realizing the dreams of India's young generation has been a moral commitment of all of us in political and social life. I express my gratitude to the Hon'ble Prime Minister for the opportunity he gave me to serve the nation under his visionary leadership," Pradhan said."Considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country — that anti-national forces should not take advantage of this situation, that the unity of the country should be preserved, that not even a single student's future should get entangled in legal complications, and that our children should devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers — I have sent my resignation to the Hon'ble Prime Minister," he added.Also Read | Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation letter Pradhan said that the government took immediate cognizance when irregularities in the NEET-UG examination came to light."However, irregularities came to light in the NEET-UG examination held on 3 May 2026. The Government of India took immediate cognizance of this, handed over the investigation to the CBI, cancelled the examination, and announced a new date for the re-examination. Alongside this, it was decided that from next year the examination would be conducted in CBT (Computer-Based Test) mode," he added.In his letter, Pradhan also accused "certain individuals" of misleading students.Also Read | 'We won't go': CJP's Dipke says protests to continue till all demands met "From the very first day, I took responsibility and never turned away from this situation. My resolve was that we would not let any meritorious student's chances be ruined because of an examination mafia, and that no injustice would be done to any student. The NEET-UG results declared on 16 July were satisfactory, with many meritorious students from poor backgrounds also achieving success," he said."However, during this time too, certain individuals occupying positions of responsibility tried to mislead students and create obstruction, which caused me deep anguish. I have always been an unwavering believer in the strength of our democracy, and I have always held deep respect for the aspirations, dreams, and expectations of the youth. They are not only India's future, but also the bearers, builders, and architects of a new and developed India," he added."Watching the events of the last 10 days has saddened me. This is not a matter of personal reputation for me. The youth power of India is the real strength of this country. My resolve is that we will not let the country's youth get caught in a web of confusion," he further said.
Article Summary: Union education minister dharmendra pradhan tendered his resignation from the council of ministers on saturday. His resignation comes amid the ongoing protests over the neet paper leak. In a letter addressed to his "young friends," prdhan said that he has sent his resignation to prime minister narendra modi.

Article Title: INS Sudarshini departs Boston for Portugal after participating in US's 250th Independence Day anniversary celebrations
Article Text:
The ministry said INS Sudarshini has now set sail for Ponta Delgada, Azores (Portugal)

NEW DELHI: Indian Navy Sailing Ship Sudarshini has set sail for Portugal, wrapping up its month-long visit to the US to participate in the celebrations of the country’s 250th anniversary of independence.“The Indian Naval Ship Sudarshini, a sail training vessel of the Indian Navy, departed Boston, US, on July 25 as part of the ongoing Lokayana 26 voyage,” a defence ministry statement said in Delhi. “Representing India at the historic SAIL250 celebrations, the IndianNavy’s sail training ship showcased the nation’s rich maritime heritage while deepening maritime partnerships,” the Navy said on X on Sunday.The ministry said INS Sudarshini has now set sail for Ponta Delgada, Azores (Portugal), continuing its journey as a beacon of India’s maritime strength, professionalism, and goodwill on the global stage.INS Sudarshini arrived at Boston on Sunday after her successful participation in the Sail4th 250 celebrations at New York. The ship took part in the Grand Parade of Sails, marking the commencement of Sail Boston 2026, the Ministry of Defence said. Raghuram Sastry, consul general of India in Boston, embarked on INS Sudarshini for the Grand Parade of Sails and the ship’s ceremonial entry into Boston.Joining an international fleet of over 60 tall ships from over 20 nations, INS Sudarshini is representing India as a maritime ambassador of goodwill during her ongoing Lokayan 2026 transoceanic expedition.INS Sudarshini is a three-masted barque, 54 metres long and has 20 sails, 7.5 km of rope and 1.5 km of steel wire rope. The ship's sails have a total area of approximately 1,035 square metres (11,140 sq ft). Capable of operations under sail or power, and with a complement of five officers, 31 sailors, and 30 cadets embarked for training, the ship can remain at sea for at least 20 days at a time.
Article Summary: Indian navy sailing ship sudarshini has set sail for portugal, wrapping up its month-long visit to the us. The ship took part in the grand parade of sails, marking the commencement of sail boston 2026. It is a three-masted barque, 54 metres long and has 20 sails, 7.5km of rope and 1.5 km of steel wire rope.

Article Title: India summons Ukraine envoy for ship attack, Kyiv seeks talks
Article Text:
Unacceptable and must be avoided: MEA

NEW DELHI: India summoned the Ukrainian ambassador Monday to condemn attacks on commercial shipping, underscoring the adverse impact of such attacks on the safety of maritime navigation, freedom of navigation and international commerce.However, Ukraine claimed it had warned India about the growing threats to civilian navigation from Russia's actions in Black Sea, saying the only sustainable way to restore maritime security was to increase international pressure on Russia to end its attacks on civilian shipping. In a statement, the Ukrainian embassy here also sought dialogue between the foreign ministers on the Black Sea security situation.Ukrainian ambassador Oleksandr Polishchuk was summoned by the MEA in connection with the attack on the commercial vessel MV Omorfi that resulted in the death of an Indian national. The ministry said it conveyed its serious concern over the incident and condemned such attacks on commercial shipping in the strongest terms."The ambassador was requested to convey to the Ukrainian authorities India's strong concerns over the targeting of commercial vessels and reiterated that such actions, which endanger the lives of innocent civilian seafarers, are unacceptable and must be avoided," the ministry said.The attacks by both Russian and Ukrainian forces on commercial shipping have caused the deaths of five Indian seafarers. In the latest such attack, a merchant vessel carrying four Indians was struck at Ukraine's port of Odesa. While two Indian crew members were confirmed safe, information about the other two is awaited.Ukrainian embassy here said in a statement that foreign minister Andrii Sybiha had written to his counterpart S Jaishankar expressing sympathy for the families of Indian seafarers who lost their lives as a result of the deteriorating security situation in the Black Sea."We hope that, following the relevant proposal made by the minister of foreign affairs of Ukraine, a conversation between the foreign ministers of our two countries will take place in the nearest future to discuss in detail the current security situation in the Black Sea region," the Ukraine statement said.According to the embassy, Ukraine had consistently warned its international partners, including senior Indian officials, about the growing threats to civilian navigation arising from Russia's actions in the Black Sea."Ukraine has also informed its partners about the measures it is taking to prevent the delivery of military cargo and disrupt logistical routes used to sustain Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine," it said.The embassy also said that timely and preventive action by competent authorities was vital to protecting seafarers, ensuring the safety of civilian navigation, and strengthening international maritime security in regions where such threats were clearly identified.
Article Summary: Ukrainian ambassador oleksandr polishchuk was summoned by the mea in connection with the attack on the commercial vessel mv omorfi that resulted in the death of an indian national. Ukraine claimed it had warned india about the growing threats to civilian navigation from russia's actions in black sea.

Article Title: 'MPs sleeping, need wake-up call': Delhi transport bodies plan Parliament march on August 4 against E20 fuel
Article Text:
E20 fuel (AI-generated image)

NEW DELHI: Delhi-based transport bodies are likely to hold a protest march to Parliament, demanding the withdrawal of ethanol-blended petrol.The planned protest would be led by the Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association along with other groups."We are planning to hold a protest march to Parliament on August 4 against ethanol-blended petrol and demand its withdrawal. We want to give a wake-up call to MPs who are sleeping on the issue, as vehicle problems linked to ethanol blending are being reported from across the country," Sanjay Samrat, president of the Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association, told PTI.He also distanced the protest call from the so-called "E-20 Janta Party" and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The CJP, an online satirical outfit, had on July 20 led a march to Parliament seeking the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET (UG) paper leak controversy, which resulted in clashes between protesters and police."We do not want to make this a political issue and are not associated with any 'E-20 Janta Party', Cockroach Janta Party or any other political party," Samrat added, referring to the online campaign against E20 fuel, which is a blend of 20% ethanol and 80% petrol.According to Harish Sabharwal, national president of the All India Motor Transport Congress, the association was protesting against the government’s move to make E20 fuel the only option available to consumers."Ethanol-blended petrol should not be forced upon commuters; there should be a choice. Currently, no option is being provided. We are supporting the protest march to Parliament, but the association has not given any call for a strike as of now," Sabharwal stated.The protest announcement comes days after the launch of the "E-20 Janata Party," an online movement formed along the lines of the CJP, which has gained a large following on Instagram and X.The E20 ethanol-blending policy has been at the centre of a major controversy, with concerns raised over reduced vehicle mileage, possible engine wear and alleged conflicts of interest.The government has defended the programme, ruling out any immediate plans to increase ethanol blending beyond 20% and maintaining that the fuel is safe, cleaner and beneficial for farmers.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth: "When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat; instead, they…" - a timeless lesson on courage, perseverance and hope in difficult times
Article Text:
Queen Elizabeth

Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth II

"When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat; instead, they are all the more determined to struggle for a better future"

Exploring the true meaning of Queen Elizabeth’s quote

Why courage often shows up in small, everyday decisions

Why staying determined matters more than an immediate win

Why hope, in this quote, is something you actually do

How the Queen's own life reflected this idea

Why hardship can build genuine strength

How to actually use this idea day to day

Other memorable quotes by Queen Elizabeth

"Grief is the price we pay for love."

"It has always been easy to hate and destroy. To build and to cherish is much more difficult."

"We all need to get the balance right between action and reflection."

"It's worth remembering that it is often the small steps, not the giant leaps, that bring about the most lasting change."

What this quote means in today’s world

Everyone goes through periods when life feels genuinely hard, illness, money worries, loss, setbacks at work, moments when the future feels uncertain. The easy response is often to give up trying. Queen Elizabeth II offered a different way of thinking about those moments in her Christmas broadcast on the 25th of December 2008. "When life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat," she said. "Instead, they are all the more determined to struggle for a better future." She was not pretending life is easy. She was simply describing what she believed made the difference between giving up and pushing on, a distinction she had plenty of occasion to think about across seven decades on the throne.The quote starts honestly, with "when life seems hard." There is no pretence here that difficulty is rare or that everyone avoids it. Everyone runs into stretches where progress feels painfully slow and obstacles seem too big to get past, whatever their circumstances happen to be.What follows is the actual point. Courage does not mean feeling no fear or no pain. It means refusing to let those feelings decide what happens next.The quote ends by pointing forward, towards "a better future," suggesting that hardship, faced properly, can actually sharpen someone's resolve rather than weaken it.People tend to picture courage as something dramatic, a single big moment of bravery. More often, it looks much smaller than that. Getting up and going back to work after a real disappointment. Asking for help during a genuinely hard time. Supporting a family through money troubles. Starting again after a business or a career falls apart. Continuing treatment through a long illness. None of these moments make headlines, yet each one takes the same basic quality, choosing to keep going anyway.A setback can feel like the end of the road, a rejected job application, a failed exam, a lost job, a broken relationship. In reality, most of these moments turn out to be turning points rather than final endings. Staying determined does not guarantee instant success. It simply keeps the door open for a future success that giving up would close for good. Someone who keeps learning and adjusting after a setback still has options that someone who quits no longer does.Hope often gets treated as just wishing things will get better on their own. This quote describes something more active. The courageous are "determined to struggle" for a better future, meaning hope only really means something once effort gets attached to it. Simply waiting for circumstances to improve is a very different thing from actually taking steps, however small, towards making that improvement happen.Elizabeth became heir to the throne during the turmoil of the Second World War and went on to reign through decades of huge social and political change. Her time as monarch included economic crises, constitutional disputes, terrorist attacks and, near the end of her reign, the Covid-19 pandemic. Across many of her speeches, she returned again and again to the same themes, endurance, duty, and the belief that difficulties can be overcome through shared effort and persistence. This particular quote fits that pattern closely.Nobody goes looking for suffering, yet difficult experiences do tend to build qualities that easier times rarely produce. Patience grows when progress is slow. Resilience develops through actually recovering from setbacks. Empathy deepens once someone has been through real struggle themselves, since it becomes much easier to recognise the same struggle in someone else. None of this glorifies hardship for its own sake. It simply recognises that adversity, met with real determination, can end up becoming a source of genuine strength rather than something that only leaves damage behind. The message reminds us that while hardship is never desirable, the character, wisdom and compassion forged through overcoming it can become some of life's most enduring strengths.Focus on the very next step rather than trying to solve the whole problem at once. Keep up routines that support your health, work and relationships, especially when things are difficult. Ask for support from family, friends or professionals rather than struggling entirely alone. Treat setbacks as something to learn from rather than proof that you have failed. And keep the long view in mind, since most difficult periods, however overwhelming they feel at the time, do eventually pass, even when it is genuinely hard to believe that while you are still in the middle of one.What makes this quote last is the balance it strikes. It never pretends suffering is not real, and it never promises every struggle will end quickly or easily. It simply offers a way of thinking about hard times, that courage is measured by the decision to keep pushing toward something better, even while the present moment still feels genuinely difficult. That is really the whole message packed into one sentence, and it explains why people keep returning to these words years after she first said them, long after the specific Christmas broadcast that produced them has been largely forgotten.
Article Summary: Queen elizabeth ii said: "when life seems hard, the courageous do not lie down and accept defeat" courage does not mean feeling no fear or no pain. It means refusing to let those feelings decide what happens next.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Alexander the Great: "I am not afraid of an army of lions led by a sheep; I am afraid of…" - a timeless lesson on leadership, courage and the power of inspiring others
Article Text:
Alexander the Great (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Alexander the Great

"I am not afraid of an army of lions led by a sheep; I am afraid of an army of sheep led by a lion"

What is the meaning behind the quote by Alexander the Great

Why the idea still matters even without a confirmed source

Why talent on its own is rarely enough

Why confidence and courage tend to spread

Why this goes well beyond the battlefield

How to actually use this idea

Other quotes attributed to Alexander the Great

"There is nothing impossible to him who will try."

"I would rather excel others in the knowledge of what is excellent than in the extent of my power."

"Heaven cannot brook two suns, nor earth two masters."

“For my part, I think that to a man of spirit there is no other aim and end of his labours except the labours themselves.”

Why this still resonates today

Numbers and weapons matter in battle, but they are rarely the whole story. Sometimes the deciding factor is simply who is standing at the front, giving the orders. That idea sits behind one of the most famous lines connected to Alexander the Great. "I am not afraid of an army of lions led by a sheep; I am afraid of an army of sheep led by a lion," the quote goes. Whether or not Alexander himself actually said these exact words, the point behind them has clearly lasted, repeated across more than two thousand years of history, passed from one century to the next long after the man himself was gone. Armies have changed beyond recognition since then, replaced by boardrooms, classrooms and sports fields, yet the underlying question stays the same: does the person in charge bring out the best in people, or waste it?The quote works through two simple pictures. An army of lions represents individually brave, capable fighters. Even so, if the person leading them lacks judgement or nerve, all that individual strength can go to waste. An army of sheep represents ordinary people, not naturally fearless, yet capable of achieving far more than expected once a genuinely strong leader is guiding them.The point is straightforward. Leadership can completely change what a group of people is able to achieve together, sometimes mattering more than the raw talent sitting inside that group.Its enduring message is that vision, confidence and effective leadership have the power to inspire ordinary people to accomplish extraordinary things together.None of that uncertainty removes the value of the idea itself. A leader does far more than hand out instructions. They build a shared sense of purpose, give people something to trust in, and help a group stay focused when things get difficult. When people genuinely believe in whoever is leading them, they often start believing more in themselves too, and that shift alone can change what an entire group manages to achieve.Plenty of teams and organisations are stacked with talented people, yet talent without real direction can produce surprisingly inconsistent results. A skilled group with no coordination or shared purpose often struggles to reach anywhere near its actual potential. This is exactly why serious organisations invest heavily in developing leadership, not just technical skill, since the two rarely produce results on their own.People frequently take their emotional cues from whoever is leading them. A calm leader during a genuine crisis tends to calm everyone else down too. A leader who clearly believes in their team's ability often ends up creating that same belief inside the people being led. Confidence, in other words, is rarely just a private, individual trait. It moves through a group, usually starting from the top.Courage works in a similar way. It has never really meant an absence of fear, only the choice to act despite it. When a leader shows that kind of courage openly, it tends to give everyone else around them permission to do the same.Although this particular image comes from warfare, the underlying lesson clearly reaches much further. Teachers shape entire classrooms. Managers shape workplaces. Coaches shape how athletes perform under pressure. Parents shape families. In every one of these settings, the quality of leadership tends to shape how people respond to real challenges and real opportunities, whether or not a battle is involved anywhere.Lead by consistent example rather than by title or authority alone. Help build confidence in others, especially during genuinely difficult moments. Focus on developing the people around you rather than simply directing their tasks. Build trust the slow way, through consistency, rather than expecting it to appear automatically. And remember that leadership itself often decides how far a group's raw ability actually gets used.Leadership remains one of the most powerful forces inside any group, whatever the century. Technology keeps changing, and the challenges people face keep getting more complicated, yet people still respond strongly to leaders who inspire genuine confidence and give others a real sense of direction. This particular saying, whoever actually said it first, has survived over two thousand years for a simple reason. Ordinary people, guided well, can end up achieving things that look nothing short of extraordinary.
Article Summary: Leading by example rather than by title or authority alone. Help build confidence in others, especially during difficult moments. Focus on you rather than simply their tasks. Don't be afraid of an army of lions led by a sheep; i am afraid of a lion. Build trust the slow way, through consistency, rather than expecting it to appear automatically.

Article Title: 'Allah commanded me': Knife-wielding man attacks 3 women on Paris street - video
Article Text: Panic gripped a busy Paris street on Monday after a man armed with two kitchen knives attacked three women in broad daylight before being overpowered by bystanders and an off-duty police officer.Two of the victims suffered severe injuries, while investigators are yet to establish the suspect's whereabouts or motive.French interior minister Laurent Nunez told reporters that the suspect attacked three women aged 19, 24 and 36 with two kitchen knives. "The man had been detained by an off-duty police officer. I pay tribute to him, it was a courageous act," Nunez said.Paris police said the attack took place at around 11:30 am local time (0930 GMT). All three victims were taken to hospital following the incident.The suspect's identity and motive remain unclear. Nunez said police had been unable to verify his identity and described his statements during arrest as 'incoherent'.Video footage first posted on Snapchat and later verified by Reuters showed a man with long black hair, wearing a cream tracksuit and wielding a large knife in each hand, attempting to attack and stab a young woman.It was not immediately clear whether the woman was injured.Another video showed the suspect lying on the ground after being restrained by members of the public, with the two knives visible nearby on a pedestrian crossing.Mohamed-Ali Bouhadjar, 26, who filmed the incident and shared the footage on Snapchat, described how bystanders intervened."When I saw him stab a woman in the back, I started shouting, 'Come on, let's stop him!' Several people stepped in," Bouhadjar told Reuters."One person threw a suitcase at him. He dropped the knives. At that moment, I grabbed him, swept his legs out from under him, and we pinned him to the ground," he said.The footage also captured the suspect making a religious statement while being restrained. "It is Allah who commanded me," the man lying on the floor says in the video.Authorities have not linked the attack to terrorism. Nunez said the motive remained unknown and reiterated that investigators were still working to establish the suspect's identity.The French national anti-terrorist prosecutor's office said it was 'in observation' over whether to open a formal investigation into the attack.The incident comes two days after an Islamist radical drove a rented minivan into a Pride parade in Berlin, killing one woman and injuring 29 others.
Article Summary: A man armed with two kitchen knives attacked three women in broad daylight. He was overpowered by bystanders and an off-duty police officer. Two of the victims suffered severe injuries, while investigators are yet to establish the suspect's whereabouts or motive.

Article Title: 'Intense, highly unpredictable': Over 200,000 evacuated as massive wildfires engulf Spain, France
Article Text:
Spain, France battle devastating wildfires

More than 200,000 people have either fled or been ordered to remain indoors as massive wildfires swept across Spain and France on Friday.The fires prompted Spain to declare a national emergency, while French authorities ordered the complete evacuation, by land and sea, of one of the country's most popular holiday destinations.Authorities in south-west France ordered the evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast "village by village" as an "intense, highly unpredictable" wildfire scorched more than 19,000 hectares (47,000 acres) of forest.In Spain, the government declared its first-ever national emergency over a wildfire after two major blazes merged outside Madrid, while a third fire was close to joining them amid extreme heat and tinder-dry conditions across much of southern Europe.Madrid regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso described the blaze as the "worst fire in the history of the region", saying the area was facing a "perfect storm" of high temperatures, relentless winds and converging fire fronts.Local emergency services said the wildfires were advancing towards the municipalities of Robledo de Chavela and Fresnedillas de la Oliva, about 50 kilometres (31 miles) from the Spanish capital."The wildfire is at its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain," Carlos Novillo, the Madrid regional government's emergency management chief, said, as cited by the BBC."It's not possible to attack the fire in that area, so defensive measures are being taken," he added.A national emergency, which allows Spain's central government to assume powers and responsibilities normally held by the country's autonomous regions, has been declared only once before — during the nationwide blackout in April 2025.In south-west France, around 200,000 people have been evacuated as wildfires tore through the Gironde and Landes regions.In the early hours of Saturday, authorities ordered the precautionary evacuation of four towns near Bordeaux: Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, Saint-Jean-d'Illac, Martignas-sur-Jalles and Saint-Aubin-de-Médoc. According to Le Monde, the four municipalities have a combined population of about 58,400.In 2022, a wildfire in south-west France scorched more than 30,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of 50,000 people. Fueled by dry conditions and strong winds, the latest blazes have swept through coastal pine forests, with flames reaching up to 10 metres (30 feet) high.French president Emmanuel Macron said he had activated the European Union's civil protection mechanism as the country battled multiple wildfires after enduring three successive heatwaves since May.Scientists say climate change is making extreme weather events more frequent and more intense by drying out soils and waterways, fuelling wildfires and contributing to thousands of excess deaths. Europe is warming at nearly twice the global average rate.
Article Summary: Spain, france battle devastating wildfires. More than 200,000 people have either fled or been ordered to remain indoors. The fires prompted spain to declare a national emergency over a wildfire. French authorities ordered the complete evacuation of one of the country's most popular holiday destinations.
